Supply chain decisions

Follow the Ripple

A decision can help one department—and still have unexpected effects somewhere else.

The decision challenge

Logistics, Sales and Procurement all have good reasons for their choices. The question is what happens beyond their own boundaries.

  1. 1
    Local objective

    What does the department hope to improve?

  2. 2
    Connected teams

    Where else might the decision create a change?

  3. 3
    System result

    What happens to cost, inventory, lead time or service?

Your task: For each of three decisions, choose one likely consequence. Then see how the effect spreads across the supply chain.

    Good decisions need a system view.

    Every department had a reasonable goal. The challenge is seeing the consequences outside its boundaries.

    Key takeaway

    A locally rational decision can become a system-wide problem when its upstream and downstream consequences are excluded.

    What the three decisions showed

    • LogisticsLower transport costs may mean longer waiting times.
    • SalesA delivery promise may increase fulfillment pressure.
    • ProcurementA volume discount may increase inventory costs.
